rows.source_body_exact: Euclidean Spin(4) is decomposed into two chiral SU(2) factors in the Euclidean-first proposal.
The two factors receive distinct gravitational/spacetime and internal-gauge roles.
Recovering Lorentz signature requires an imaginary-time-direction degree of freedom assigned a Higgs role.
Projective twistor space is the proposed natural base of the Euclidean-first theory.
The twistor construction supplies internal U(1) and SU(3) structure.
The proposal contains a construction for one Standard Model generation.
Minkowski conformal/twistor geometry uses SU(2,2) / Spin(4,2) structure.
The 2023 formulation replaces the chirally symmetric complex-spacetime description with a purely right-handed Lorentz action.
In that formulation, Euclidean left-handed spinors acquire an internal SU(2) role.
A distinguished Euclidean vector can reconstruct an isomorphism between left-handed and conjugate right-handed spinors, relating asymmetric and symmetric descriptions.
The usual Wick rotation of a single Weyl field creates a Euclidean chirality/doubling problem.
W04a proposes using only the right-handed spinor kind for spacetime vectors in both Minkowski and Euclidean signatures.
Under W04a, SU(2)_R acts geometrically and SU(2)_L is available as an internal symmetry.
Twistor space is C^4 / projective CP^3 with an SU(2,2) real form giving positive, negative, and null/boundary orbits for the Minkowski picture.
Euclidean spacetime is associated with extra fibration/real-structure data rather than the same real form as Minkowski spacetime.
W04c explicitly records a change from Euclidean-first to Minkowski-twistor-first foundational viewpoint.
In W04c, Wick rotation becomes a gauge-like extra choice, and the left chiral symmetry is interpreted internally before that choice.
W04c leaves the electroweak/Higgs completion of the revised viewpoint unresolved.
W04d identifies complex-time holomorphy / boundary values as the essence of Wick rotation and says there is no distinguished Euclidean target without extra structure.
W04d explicitly states that the exact new Wick-rotation implementation remains unresolved.
W04e says the author's interpretation is still changing and therefore later claims must remain revision-scoped.
W04e proposes a new conjugation-like structure interchanging positive/negative imaginary-time sectors while preserving a Lorentzian-chiral subspace.
In Euclidean twistor geometry, a spacetime point is represented by a twistor P1.
W05 presents the twistor P1 as a geometric avatar of quaternions.
W03 is mutable project-status evidence and cannot overwrite frozen source revisions without an explicit successor target.
W01 fixes the Euclidean vector real form inside M(2,C) by the Pauli-matrix map, with determinant equal to positive Euclidean norm squared and an equivalent quaternion presentation with x KAPPA(x).
W01 represents Spin(4) by independent left/right SU(2)=Sp(1) actions, with the Euclidean vector action x -> g_L x g_R^{-1}; the two factors are structurally independent in Euclidean signature.

W01 identifies the common complexification of Euclidean, Minkowski, and split-signature four-vector spaces with M(2,C)=Hom(S_R,S_L), while retaining different real-form/action constraints for each signature.

W01's frame-bundle description distinguishes spin-connection one-forms omega from canonical/frame one-forms e, takes e and omega as the fundamental Palatini fields, and writes the action as the integral of epsilon_ABCD e^A wedge e^B wedge Omega^CD(omega); its equations of motion are obtained by varying omega^AB, which gives de^A + omega^A_B wedge e^B = 0 and thereby the torsion-free Levi-Civita connection determined by e, and by varying e^A, which gives the Einstein equations in terms of e.
W01 decomposes spin connection, curvature, and two-forms into chiral/Hodge sectors; the right and left connection-curvature pairs act on S_R and S_L respectively.

For a torsion-free connection W01 states the vacuum Einstein condition as vanishing of a specified mixed/chiral curvature component and motivates a chiral formulation using only the right-handed connection/curvature sector; the omitted left connection becomes unconstrained if torsion is allowed.

W01 constructs the weak SU(2)_L gauge sector from the left spin connection and uses the imaginary-time component of the canonical one-form as a Higgs candidate; it explicitly records the missing electroweak U(1) and SU(2)_R-invariance problems that motivate the twistor-space reformulation.
W01 identifies Euclidean projective twistor space CP3 -> S4 as the bundle whose CP1/S2 fiber parametrizes orthogonal complex structures J on each R4 tangent space, with J^2=-1.

For a chosen orthogonal complex structure J, W01 decomposes R4 tensor C into +i/-i eigenspaces and constructs S_R and S_L through exterior powers; the stabilizer U(2) lifts to SU(2)_L x U(1) with U(1) inside SU(2)_R.
On PT the lifted spinor roles have U(1) weights S_L=C^2_0 and S_R=C_-1 + C_+1 under SU(2)_L x U(1).

W01 defines the tautological line L over PT and the rank-3 quotient L^perp=C4/L; PT is SU(4)/S(U(1)xU(3)), SU(3) acts on L^perp as the color group, and the determinant-one condition fixes the relative U(1) weights.

W01 represents one Standard Model generation by Hom(l + l^perp, S_R + S_L), whose SU(3)xSU(2)_LxU(1) decomposition reproduces the listed quark/lepton transformation roles including a right-handed neutrino.

W01 explicitly distinguishes this construction from conventional GUT unification: it does not place all gauge groups into one larger Lie group and does not identify a generation with a single usual GUT spinor representation.
In W01 the U(1) and SU(3) gauge principal bundles are intrinsic to PT rather than pullbacks from S4; a full interacting theory on PT is explicitly left undeveloped.

W01 identifies the t=0 compactified Minkowski S3 with the equator of Euclidean S4 and the null PT_0 locus Phi(s,s)=0; upper/lower Euclidean hemispheres correspond to positive/negative imaginary-time regions.
For free massless spinors W01 uses the Penrose transform H^1(PT_+,O(-3)) <-> Weyl solutions on S4_+ and fiber restriction H^1(CP1,O(-3))=C2 to reconstruct pointwise spinor values.

W01 states the Penrose-Ward correspondence between anti-self-dual gauge connections on spacetime regions and holomorphic vector bundles on twistor regions, with the explicit limitation that this directly covers anti-self-dual rather than general Yang-Mills fields.

W01 requires any future PT quantum theory to relate fields on the five-dimensional PT_0 fibered over S3 to ordinary state data on S3 and notes that the intrinsic PT gauge bundles vary along CP1 fibers, so ordinary pullback correspondence is insufficient.
W01's open-problem section keeps the origin of three generations unresolved and treats S7/unit-octonion/Spin(8)/G2 possibilities as speculation rather than established structure.

W01 speculates that the 4x4-complex-matrix generation construction may be a lift of the Clifford-algebra bundle on S4 and contrasts it with ordinary Kogut-Susskind multiplicity; this is not part of the established PT construction.

W01 leaves the gauge-theory/spinor-field quantization formalism on PT unresolved and mentions anti-self-dual/twistor-action and supersymmetric/twisted theories only as possible clues, not as adopted dynamics.

Appendix A identifies compactified complex spacetime with G_2,4(C), its tautological rank-2 bundle S and quotient S^perp, and tangent bundle TM=Hom(S,S^perp); the Klein relation omega wedge omega=0 embeds the Grassmannian into projective Lambda^2(C4).
Appendix A defines the line-plane incidence relation s^perp=Zs and the fractional-linear SL(4,C) action Z -> (C+DZ)(A+BZ)^-1; the correspondence space P(S) links PT and M.
Appendix A defines alpha-planes from a twistor point and states that two spacetime points incident with the same projective twistor have null separation in the determinant quadratic form.
Appendix A distinguishes the Penrose transform for massless helicity equations from the Penrose-Ward extension with gauge fields, including open-set and fiber-triviality side conditions.

Appendix A distinguishes split, Minkowski, Euclidean, and compact SU(4) real-form structures of SL(4,C), each with different fixed/orbit/signature conditions; these real forms may not be collapsed into one representation.
For Minkowski twistor geometry W01 uses a signature-(2,2) Hermitian form Phi, anti-Hermitian affine coordinates, the SU(2,2) orbit decomposition of M/PT, and conjugate-dual left/right spinor actions.

For Euclidean twistor geometry W01 uses T=H^2, the pseudoreal map sigma with sigma^2=-1 on T and +1 projectively, HP1 homogeneous coordinates, SL(2,H) fractional-linear action, and the CP1 fibration whose sigma action is antipodal on each fiber.

Appendix B treats reconstruction of physical states from Euclidean data as requiring a chosen imaginary-time half-space/reflection and states that the resulting distinction between positive and negative imaginary time breaks SO(4) despite SO(4)-invariant Schwinger functions.

Appendix B gives the single-Weyl-field obstruction: a one-chirality Euclidean path-integral/Lagrangian cannot be made SO(4)-invariant in the conventional construction without opposite chirality/doubling; this motivates the source's alternative interpretation.

Appendix C treats Wightman/distribution data as boundary-value/hyperfunction structure and makes positive/negative holomorphic-domain decomposition load-bearing to the source's analytic-continuation discussion.

W03 records the project chronology as a succession of Euclidean-twistor, right-handed-spacetime, and July-2026 Wick-rotation/chiral-field stages; these are revision relations, not one timeless formulation.

The July-2026 W03 status explicitly says the current notes are work in progress, are unlikely to be updated in place, and a future write-up is expected to differ significantly; mutable status evidence therefore cannot retroactively rewrite W01/W02.

W04a writes a right-handed Minkowski Weyl equation of the form (E-sigma dot p) psi_R=0, derives the Klein-Gordon mass-shell consequence, and associates its positive- and negative-energy branches with opposite helicities. It prints the energy-momentum equation (E-sigma·p) tilde_psi_R(E,p)=0, the ordered factorization (E+sigma·p)(E-sigma·p)=E^2-|p|^2, the conditional mass shell E=±|p|, and the helicity operator (1/2)(sigma·p)/|p| with +1/2 for positive-energy particles and -1/2 for negative-energy antiparticles; these are source-written roles, not qualified lower physical laws.

W04a passes from the classical Weyl equation to the quantum oscillator/field description and treats Standard-Model copies, gauge-covariant derivatives, and Higgs/Yukawa mass couplings as additional matter structure rather than part of the bare spacetime representation.

W04a contrasts the right-handed Minkowski Wightman kernel with the naive Euclidean substitution and makes the failure of a one-chirality Euclidean propagator/Lagrangian a concrete Wick-rotation obstruction. The displayed source Wightman formula is tilde_W2(E,p)=(E-sigma·p)^(-1)=(E+sigma·p)/(E^2-|p|^2), while the candidate naive Schwinger continuation is tilde_S2(E,p)=(iE-sigma·p)^(-1). The second is expressly an unsuccessful conventional Wick-rotation attempt, not an established continuation; the source's conventional vector operator is a map from S_R^* to S_L and the proposed right-handed-only replacement is separate.

In the conventional four-dimensional spinor-vector description W04a represents a complex vector as a map from the dual right spinor to the left spinor; Minkowski reality relates the two chiralities by conjugation whereas Euclidean signature leaves them independent.

W04a states that conventional Osterwalder-Schrader treatment of one Weyl field introduces the opposite Euclidean chirality and an additional doubling, so the source does not regard ordinary analytic continuation as preserving the minimal chiral carrier.

The W04a alternative builds spacetime vectors from the right-handed spinor and its conjugate in both signatures, so only SU(2)_R acts geometrically on Euclidean vectors while SU(2)_L is available as an internal symmetry.
W04a identifies the right-handed spinor plane appearing in the vector construction with the tautological right-handed plane used to represent a twistor spacetime point.

W04b treats complexified four-dimensional spacetime as the common carrier for SL(2,C)_L x SL(2,C)_R and distinguishes Minkowski and Euclidean real forms by different real subgroup conditions rather than by identifying their chiral factors. W04b prints Spin(4,C)=SL(2,C)_L×SL(2,C)_R; its Minkowski real-form embedding is g∈SL(2,C)↦(conjugate(g),g) with conjugation on the FIRST factor, and its Euclidean preserving group is printed Spin(4)=SU(2)_L×SU(2)_R. Do not swap factor order, remove conjugation, add an inverse/adjoint not printed here, or normalize the group presentation.
W04b uses T=C4, PT=CP3, and projective CP1 data to describe spacetime points and presents the one-complex-dimensional CP1 case as an instructive lower-dimensional real-form/orbit analogue.
In the CP1 analogue W04b uses the three SU(1,1)=SL(2,R) orbits and hyperfunction boundary values to model the relation between holomorphic domains and Lorentzian boundary data.
In four dimensions W04b uses the SU(2,2)=Spin(4,2) action on PT with positive, negative, and null orbits; compactified Minkowski points are represented by CP1s contained in the null orbit.
W04b invokes Penrose-transform holomorphic data on the open twistor orbits and boundary-value data on the null orbit as the source-side analogue of complex-time continuation.

For the Euclidean real form W04b uses SL(2,H)=Spin(5,1), C4=H2, and the CP3 -> HP1=S4 fibration with CP1 fibers; Wick rotation requires choosing such a Euclidean fibration and its intersection with the Minkowski null geometry.

W04c promotes the PT+/PT-/null-orbit holomorphic/boundary picture from an analogy to the proposed fundamental starting point, while stating that a gravitational theory must abandon or deform the global SU(2,2) structure.
W04c interprets Wick rotation as an extra choice of CP1 fibration/imaginary-time direction rather than a fundamental Euclidean-to-Minkowski coordinate substitution.
W04c explicitly revises the Euclidean-first program into a Minkowski-twistor/holomorphic-first viewpoint and treats Euclidean geometry as a chosen realization of more primitive complex-twistor data.

In the revised W04c role assignment SL(2,C)_R acts on the twistor CP1 point data while the left factor acts on the tangent space to the space parametrizing the CP1s; after the Wick-rotation choice an SU(2)_L role is interpreted internally.
W04c proposes that the choice involved in Wick rotation can break the internal SU(2)_L role, but explicitly says the complete electroweak/Higgs formalism has not been recovered.

W04c retains Penrose and Penrose-Ward structures and proposes the canonical line and rank-three quotient bundles on CP3 as sources of U(1) and SU(3) internal structure, with matter described by holomorphic or Dolbeault-type data.
W04c leaves the generation problem, the correct Dirac-versus-Dolbeault operator, interacting dynamics, and much of the proposed holomorphic field theory unresolved.

W04d identifies the spectral positivity of time evolution with holomorphy of U(z)=exp(-izH) in a complex-time half-plane and treats this holomorphic-domain structure as the operational core of Wick rotation. W04d explicitly writes U(t)=e^(-itH), z=t+is and U(z)=e^(-izH), and attributes holomorphy to energy positivity in the LOWER complex-time half-plane (s<0); the negative-imaginary-time axis is only one possible restriction, not a unique Wick-rotation target.
W04d transfers the half-plane/boundary picture to the twistor split PT+, PT-, PT0 and proposes holomorphic data on an open twistor domain with physical boundary data on PT0.
W04d says a Euclidean realization requires additional quaternionic/fibration structure and explicitly leaves the exact new spinor/twistor Wick-rotation implementation unresolved.

The W04e notes reject ordinary inverse Wick rotation as the fundamental operation for a chiral theory because complexification introduces the opposite chirality and does not preserve the physical Hermitian structure.

W04e instead uses an antilinear reflection/conjugation Theta associated with imaginary-time reflection in Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction; the Hilbert-space inner product and physical state space are reconstructed from this reflection-positive Euclidean structure.

The W04e reconstruction requires choosing an imaginary-time half-space/direction and reflection, so the physical-state reconstruction breaks Euclidean SO(4) even when the underlying Euclidean correlation data are SO(4)-covariant.

W04e develops a two-dimensional chiral analogue in which a purely chiral Euclidean theory is related to chiral Minkowski data by a choice of conjugation/equator rather than by ordinary analytic continuation that doubles chiral variables.

W04e applies the same structural proposal in four dimensions: begin with a right-handed holomorphic Euclidean/twistor theory and recover chiral Lorentzian data by a chosen conjugation/real structure instead of adding an independent opposite-chirality Euclidean field.

In the twistor version W04e uses a Hermitian form Phi to split projective twistor space into positive, negative, and null regions; holomorphic theory on PT+ is proposed to have boundary values on the null region representing chiral Minkowski data, with Penrose/Penrose-Ward constructions supplying part of the reconstruction machinery.

W04e retains the right-handed spacetime/internal-SU(2)_L role split and the canonical-line/quotient-bundle route toward electroweak/color structure, but explicitly remains preliminary and leaves the full dynamics and Higgs realization unresolved.

The W04d slide deck gives the conventional Wick-rotation route as positive-energy tube holomorphy plus Spin(4,C)/locality continuation and states that physical-state reconstruction from Euclidean data still requires a chosen imaginary-time direction/Osterwalder-Schrader reflection.

W04d explicitly contrasts the conventional complex vector carrier S_L tensor S_R with the proposed right-handed carrier S_R tensor conjugate(S_R); on the Euclidean slice the latter decomposes as a scalar plus a three-vector and SU(2)_L acts trivially.

W04d identifies conformally compactified complex spacetime with Gr(2,4,C), a spacetime point with a right-handed C2 plane in T=C4, and projective twistor space with CP3 containing the corresponding CP1.
W04d lists SU(4), SL(4,R), SL(2,H), and SU(2,2) as real forms of SL(4,C)=Spin(6,C), with the SL(2,H) and SU(2,2) forms assigned Euclidean and Minkowski geometric roles respectively.

Under the SU(2,2) real form W04d defines PT+, PT-, and PT0 by the sign of a signature-(2,2) Hermitian form; compactified Minkowski points are CP1s lying in PT0, and PT0 is the space of Minkowski light rays/celestial spheres.
Under the Euclidean SL(2,H) real form W04d uses T=C4=H2 and the CP3->HP1=S4 fibration sending each complex line to the quaternionic line it generates.

W04d gives two equivalent geometric roles for Euclidean PT: the projective right-spin bundle and the bundle of orthogonal complex structures on S4; it states that the latter construction extends to four-dimensional Riemannian manifolds and becomes a complex twistor space for anti-self-dual metrics.

W04d closes by proposing positive-energy Minkowski physics as PT0 boundary values of quantities holomorphic on PT+, with a chosen imaginary-time direction yielding a Euclidean twistor theory; the associated SU(2)_L-as-internal/spontaneously-broken interpretation is explicitly work in progress.

W05 defines a real structure on CP1 as an antiholomorphic map rho: CP1 -> CP1 with rho squared equal to 1. The ordinary real structure is complex conjugation rho([z1,z2])=[bar(z1),bar(z2)]; its real points are exactly the points fixed by rho, forming a circle in CP1 (the real line in the affine z coordinate). W05 explicitly contrasts this ordinary real structure with the twistor antipodal real structure rho_tw, defined by rho_tw([z1,z2])=[-bar(z2),bar(z1)] (equivalently rho_tw(z)=-1/bar(z)); on C2 coordinates rho_tw squared equals -1, while on projective points rho_tw squared equals 1, and on the sphere rho_tw is the antipodal map with no projective fixed points. W05 also presents the same twistor P1 as the real projective conic x^2+y^2+z^2=0 in projective two-space, defined over the real numbers, with complex points but no real points. W05 explicitly identifies the Riemann sphere CP1 with complex lines in C2: homogeneous [z1,z2] denotes an equivalence class of pairs of complex numbers, and the affine coordinate chart z=z1/z2 identifies C with CP1 minus the point [z1,0]. For ordinary conjugation W05 also gives rho(z)=bar(z) in this affine chart. For the twistor map, W05 explicitly shows that the fixed-point equation z=-1/bar(z) would imply |z|^2=-1, a contradiction for a complex number. W05 furthermore describes the twistor P1 as the complex projective variety CP1 equipped with an action of Gal(C/R) and separately as the equation-defined real projective conic; these are its two source-given presentations. W05 writes the ordinary homogeneous real-point fixed-point equation rho([z1,z2])=[z1,z2] as the criterion for a real point of the ordinary structure. W05 also explicitly states that no projective point satisfies the homogeneous twistor fixed-point equation rho_tw([z1,z2])=[z1,z2]; this equation occurs under the source's negated existence claim, not as an asserted positive fixed point. In this W05 §2 source statement, rho_tw is itself the declared antiholomorphic CP1 real-structure MAP with source-given homogeneous arguments and outputs, not an optional relation restricted to witnessed two-step applications. Its map-type CP1 domain/codomain, projective-square identity, and projective fixed-point nonexistence are separate source obligations; the coordinate-level square-minus-identity and affine formula are distinct carrier/chart clauses and do not replace the projective type law.

W05 derives rho_tw from the chosen H=C2 presentation by left multiplication by quaternion j and uses the same quaternionic mechanism on C4=H2 to define the Euclidean projective-twistor real structure.  W05 writes the coordinate representation x0+x1i+x2j+x3k in H ↔ (x0+x1i,x2+x3i) in C2, takes z1=x0+x1i and z2=x2+x3i, and writes q=z1+z2j. Its printed multiplication chain gives j(z1+z2j)=j(x0+x1i)+j(x2+x3i)j=-(x2-x3i)+(x0-x1i)j=-bar(z2)+bar(z1)j. This is the source's explicit anti-conjugate coordinate behavior of left multiplication by j, not an imported quaternion-law proof.

W05 states that rho_tw on CP3 has no fixed projective points but has a four-real-dimensional family of invariant CP1 real lines parametrized by HP1=S4; each such line is a twistor P1.  W05 identifies PT=CP3 as complex lines in T=C4=H2 and explicitly gives the ordinary CP3 map rho([z1,z2,z3,z4])=[bar(z1),bar(z2),bar(z3),bar(z4)] and twistor map rho_tw([z1,z2,z3,z4])=[-bar(z2),bar(z1),-bar(z4),bar(z3)]. Ordinary rho has real-point space RP3 of real dimension three; rho_tw has no real points but preserves a four-real-dimensional family of projective CP1 lines that are real lines. W05 presents HP1=S4 through quaternion pairs [q1,q2] as homogeneous equivalence classes, with affine ordered quotient q=(q2)^-1 q1 identifying H with HP1 minus [q1,0]. The explicit map pi:[z1,z2,z3,z4] in CP3 -> [z1+z2j,z3+z4j] in HP1 takes each complex line to its generated quaternionic line; its fibers are exactly the CP1 real lines for rho_tw. Each fiber is a twistor P1 on which the restricted rho_tw acts as in W05 §2.

W05 contrasts Euclidean and Minkowski reality: the Euclidean twistor real structure acts on PT itself and preserves the CP1 fibers, while the Minkowski reality structure naturally maps PT to its dual and interchanges spinor chirality.  W05 additionally says the usual and twistor maps rho,rho_tw are the only two inequivalent real structures on CP3 in the declared scope. The linear action of SL(2,C) on C2 induces a conformal action on CP1 not commuting with its real structure; the SL(2,H)=Spin(5,1) action on C4=H2 similarly induces a CP3 action not commuting with rho_tw. Minkowski points of Gr(2,4,C) require a different real structure that maps PT=CP3 to its projective dual PT*, whereas Euclidean rho_tw acts on PT itself; the Minkowski relation exchanges the two spinor chiralities.

W05 gives the noncompact Euclidean twistor space R4 x CP1 the complex structure determined fiberwise by the selected orthogonal complex structure and identifies the holomorphic fibration with O(1) direct-sum O(1); for quaternionic dimension d this becomes 2d copies of O(1).  W05 gives orthogonal complex structures on R4=H by the unit imaginary quaternion x1i+x2j+x3k with x=(x1,x2,x3) a unit vector; these structures form a CP1 sphere. The map pi:R4 x CP1 -> CP1 is projection to the second factor; the total space carries the complex structure selected on R4 by the CP1 coordinate and the usual one on CP1, making pi holomorphic. Its real structure is identity on R4 and rho_tw on CP1. The holomorphic bundle is O(1) direct-sum O(1). W05 provides a separate construction using the matrices x1 sigma1+x2 sigma2+x3 sigma3 for x unit: the +1 eigenspace of this matrix on C2 above each x yields O(1). Two such copies yield O(1) direct-sum O(1) with total space R4 x CP1 and fiber R4 identified with C direct-sum C=C2, generalized to a quaternionic vector space of dimension d as 2d copies of O(1). W05 also gives the correspondence between self-dual Yang-Mills connections on S4 and holomorphic bundle structures on CP3 and describes the self-dual Einstein/nonlinear-graviton extension.

W05 records the hyperkahler generalization as a sphere aI+bJ+cK of compatible complex/Kahler structures and relates the corresponding twistor spaces to hyperkahler quotients and moduli spaces generated from self-dual Yang-Mills and its dimensional reductions.  W05's source-given hyperkahler carrier is a manifold M of real dimension 4k with three compatible Kahler structures I,J,K obeying IJ=K and a sphere of combinations aI+bJ+cK for (a,b,c) on the unit sphere in R3. Examples include H^k, complex Lie-group coadjoint orbits, flat GL(n,C) connection moduli and Higgs-bundle moduli on a Riemann surface. Hyperkahler quotient by group G generalizes symplectic reduction; self-dual Yang-Mills connections on R4 modulo gauge transformations produce finite-dimensional moduli. Invariance in one direction yields monopoles/Bogomolny solutions, in two directions Higgs/Hitchin solutions, and in three directions complex coadjoint orbits/Nahm solutions. These are source-mentioned constructions, not qualified internal definitions.

W05 presents Simpson's twistor-structure description of a pure real Hodge structure as a U(1)-equivariant holomorphic bundle on the twistor P1, with bundle degree/slope and the U(1) weights encoding the Hodge filtration.  W05 writes the Hodge decomposition H^n(M,C)=directsum_(p+q=n) H^(p,q)(M) and source-printed pure real weight-w Hodge filtration F^p with conjugate-complement condition F^p directsum conjugate(F^(n-p+1))=V. Its CP1 holomorphic bundle classification uses direct sums of line bundles O(w), while the twistor-real counterparts have rank two for odd degree w and rank one for even w, denoted O_(P1_tw)(w/2) with slope w/2. For V of dimension n the pure twistor E is a direct sum of n copies of O_(P1_tw)(w/2) and Hodge filtration corresponds to a U(1) action on E. W05 uses the coordinate lambda=1/z near infinity, the trivial E1=V tensor_R O_(P1_tw) away from lambda=0, and gluing with an E2 near lambda=0 using F^p. Conversely the U(1) weight spaces at lambda=0 recover the associated graded of F^p. W05's table separately pairs real Hodge structure with U(1)-equivariant twistor bundle; weight w with O_(P1_tw)(w/2) sums; underlying V with E1; and filtration with modification of E1 at infinity. These source formulas and ordered correspondences are not asserted as arbitrary lower module laws. W05 also states that although the Hodge decomposition does not vary holomorphically with changing complex structure, its filtration does. The printed decreasing-filtration chain begins 0 subset F^n subset F^(n-1) subset ... subset F^1 and concludes with an F^2=V symbol as actually printed; this unusual terminal superscript is conserved as source text without silently substituting a conventional filtration bound or claiming internal consistency. The explicit source complement is F^p directsum conjugate(F^(n-p+1))=V, and the source-printed formula gives F^p as the direct sum of H^q(M,Omega^i) over i STRICTLY GREATER than p (i>p), not i>=p; the source also prints H^(p,q)(M) = F^p intersect conjugate(F^q) under that same Hodge paragraph; the source also states the mixed Hodge case is excluded here.

W05 presents the non-abelian Hodge example in which the hyperkahler moduli space is viewed over CP1 through lambda-connections, with lambda=1 giving ordinary flat connections and lambda=0 giving Higgs bundles.  W05 writes the representation moduli as M=H^1(X,GL(n,C)) for equivalence classes of representations pi1(X)->GL(n,C); it explicitly treats M as a set, not a vector space, and states that these non-abelian coefficients do not extend this construction to higher-degree cohomology. For X=Sigma a Riemann surface this moduli is hyperkahler, with CP1 twistor descriptions connecting Higgs-bundle, holomorphic-flat-connection and fundamental-group-representation moduli. The source's Deligne lambda-connection parameter is a complex coordinate on CP1, with lambda=1 giving ordinary connections and lambda=0 giving Higgs bundles; these are distinct source instances.

W05 generalizes the real quaternion algebra to quaternion algebras (a,b/F), distinguishes split and division classes by the Hilbert symbol, and notes that the real split and quaternion classes become isomorphic after complex scalar extension.  W05 also defines for x=n/m in Q the p-adic norm |x|_p=p^(-a), where a is the p-power in its factorization; Qp is the completion with respect to |.|_p and R the infinite-prime completion. Over a field F the generalized quaternion algebra has basis 1,i,j,k and printed relations ij=-ji=k, i^2=a, j^2=b, for invertible a,b, denoted (a,b/F). H=(-1,-1/R); over R the split class M(2,R) and H are nonisomorphic but satisfy H tensor_R C = M(2,R) tensor_R C = M(2,C). Over Qp the split class M(2,Qp) and division class (p,u/Qp) are distinct for u a nonsquare unit; in a quadratic extension K the classes become M(2,K). The Hilbert symbol (a,b)_F is +1 exactly for (a,b/F) isomorphic to M(2,F), and -1 otherwise. These field, quotient and case distinctions are explicitly source-written. W05 enumerates for p not equal to 2 exactly three named quadratic extensions of Qp: Qp[sqrt(p)], Qp[sqrt(u)], and Qp[sqrt(up)] for u a nonsquare p-adic unit. The source prints the scalar-extension equality (p,u/Qp) tensor_Qp K = M(2,Qp) tensor_Qp K = M(2,K), showing the formerly distinct split and division classes agree over such K; neither arbitrary extension independence nor field-existence laws are imported.

W05 associates quaternion-algebra classes with projective conics and uses the no-F-rational-point/fixed-point-free Galois action as the finite-prime analogue of the twistor P1 antipodal real structure.
